v1 98.893/98.745. THREE NEIGHBOURS, a struck-metal techno gamelan at 124 bpm in 7-limit just intonation on D (1 9/8 7/6 4/3 3/2 14/9 7/4).
- THE RING: an elementary cellular automaton on 16 cells, one row a bar. Every live cell strikes a physical-model bar on its sixteenth: modal marimba, vibes, glock, a church bell tolling every 8 bars, a gong at each change of rule, and modal membrane toms on the deaths.
- The RULE changes by section: 90 (a Sierpinski triangle growing from one cell: glock, then marimba), 30 (chaos), 110 (gliders, in half time on glock and vibes with septimal 6:7:9 chords ringing), 184 (traffic: the pattern rotates, a canon, no kick), then 30 and 90 together at the peak, and 4 (only loners survive) in the decay and out.
- The population picks the chord root every 4 bars (D, A, G or the 7/4 C) and rotates the Euclidean hats and the Karplus-Strong bass. Chance (?p) decides which births and deaths sound on each render.
- A tanpura drone holds the tuning.
Structure: rule 30 and 110 merged into one section until the glider got its own floor (half-time kick, sustained bass); 11 sections, structure 100. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1; renders at about 0.1 of real time on 2 threads. (Not queued.)
next: Spectrum (90): band 21; an intro that meets t2's tail; a voice? (t6 holds the voice cluster).

v2 96.427/96.196 (v1 rescored on 8ef47431 95.972/95.639). THE MACHINE TUNES ITSELF (T3_R2=live), on wM's tunings, complex systems and morph.
- The notes are now written in plain 12-TET D minor, and the song tuning ramps from 12-TET into the 7-limit just scale over ten bars from the boot. F, Bb and C sag a third of a semitone into the septimal minor third, sixth and harmonic seventh as you listen. Chords are the scale's own sevenths (the D one is 1 7/6 3/2 7/4).
- A SELF-WRITING DRUM MACHINE joins: chirp's own cellular automaton (gen ca) plays a percussion kit in the glider (rule 110, random start) and the peak (rule 30), a second ring beside the written one.
- A LORENZ attractor (a song var with a system) swirls the vibes' filter and the glock's stereo place.
- In the TRAFFIC break the rotating marimba canon MORPHS into the tanpura's spectrum and back (morph keyed by the drone, 0 -> 0.75 -> 0).
Cohesion 93 -> 100, spectrum 90.7 -> 91.8, 12 sections. Flow 39 (t2 and t4 now exist; the seams to meet next). -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

WHOLE round. v4 97.402/97.362 (v3 rescored now 97.057/96.941). THE HYMN (T3_R4=hymn): the cell's line becomes a real tune and the peak stops standing still.
- The peak (38 bars, sections w7-w9 static) is now 18 bars, and a new 16-bar HYMN follows it: the cell's song in full, a sung DUET (the clear voice on the tune, the rounder voice a third or a sixth under, separate humanized takes): "I only know the two beside me / what I become is what we were / I only know the two beside me / and they are enough" (a cell's next state is what it and its two neighbours were).
- For the first time in the song the harmony is WRITTEN, not picked by the population: Dm Bb F Dm | Gm C F Bb | Dm Bb Am Am | Bb C Dm Dm, snapped into the septimal JI (the Bb chord is 9/7 + 7/6). It is played on a HARMONIUM (new to the album) with a walking pluck bass, and the automaton keeps running quietly underneath.
- The tune is FORESHADOWED in A (w3, static before), augmented, on a KORA (also new to the album). The kora remembers "and they are enough" in the decay, and the low voice sings it alone in the out: the last words.
- THREE NEIGHBOURS LEFT: the decay starts from three isolated cells (D, F, 14/9 Bb) and entropy takes them until the 14/9 bar (~913 Hz) is left. It is struck plainly in the last bar: the ring t4 opens by catching, now deterministic.
- Mix: the voices measured on a no-loudness copy sit ~5 dB under the band, the kora ~6 dB under. A 600 Hz cut on the new parts plus a master 750 Hz dip: spectrum 91.8 -> 95.7.
-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

- THE RULES RING: the peak's two automata, rule 30 (marimba) and rule 90 (glock), have their RULE NUMBERS played as bell patterns. Each rule's eight output bits (neighbourhoods 111 down to 000) become eight eighths: rule 30 = 0 0 0 1 1 1 1 0 on a high agogo, rule 90 = 0 1 0 1 1 0 1 0 on a low one. They interlock like a West African bell pair or a kotekan.
- The pattern is built in four-bar blocks across the window: high bell; + low bell; + shekere; then both bells doubled into sixteenths, so the static peak now climbs into the hymn's drop.
- The library's afro-perc, new to the album. New tracks only. sections --against: w7 residual -10.6 dB, w8 -40.7 (hall tail), the rest -53.

PALETTE round. v8 97.517/97.511 (v7 rescored on 03b601e2 97.361/97.373). T3_R8=kotekan.
- A GAMELAN GANGSA (the library's shimmering Balinese bronze keys, their paired tuning beating; new to the album) plays KOTEKAN with the marimba: the interlock where one part fills exactly the gaps of the other.
- The marimba strikes the live cells; the gangsa strikes the dead cells that have a live neighbour. The neighbourhood itself, the two beside each cell, is made audible. Composite sixteenths in both rule-30 sections (A and the peak), so it returns.
- The backbeat rim leaves machine-kit's clap for a djembe slap, with the hand drums. machine-kit now only keeps the kick and the open hat.
- Mix: the gangsa's 1-2 kHz tipped spectrum 96 -> 94, so it gets a 1.5 kHz cut plus a gentle master dip at 1.3 kHz: spectrum 97.6. Gangsa ~8 dB under the marimba.
